elements.element: Customer is subject to no non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and expressly acknowledges that Customer made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 affirmatively permits Customer to develop, market, sell, or acquire competing products or services.

elements.element: Customer is subject to no field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction must be limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so there is no broader restriction requiring limitation to a named product.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction must apply during the term only.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction or restricted period remains, including during or after the term.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction must be capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so its duration is zero and does not exceed 12 months.

elements.element: Customer's internal development activities must be carved out from any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 permits Customer to develop any product or service, and Section 12.4 specifically permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Customer's acquisitions must be carved out from any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 expressly permit Customer to acquire any product or service, including one that competes with Vendor.

result.reason: The redline removes the operative worldwide, all-product, 24-month post-term non-compete and replaces it with an affirmative permission consistent with Section 12.3. It fully achieves the preferred position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied because no restriction remains and internal development and acquisitions are expressly permitted. The change is confined to the conflicting non-compete provision, preserves unrelated terms, and introduces no contradiction, though Sections 12.3 and 12.4 are somewhat redundant.
